questions.q: What actually changes about the star schema when moving from a small dataset to a massive one?
options: Not the shape — a fact table with conformed dimensions is still the right default; what changes is what it costs to scan, join, and update
The star schema stops working entirely and must be replaced
Dimensions are no longer needed at scale
Fact tables become dimension tables at scale
questions.explain: The modeling idea from T-SQL Lessons 113-116 doesn't change — the cost of scanning and joining at scale is a system design problem, not a modeling one.

questions.q: Why must a fact table's grain be fixed before choosing between star and snowflake schema?
options: Because every dimension and query built on top assumes that grain — getting it wrong later requires a redesign, not a tweak
Grain only matters for snowflake schemas, not star schemas
Grain is decided automatically by the database engine
Grain has no real effect on row counts or joins
questions.explain: "One row per order" versus "one row per order line item" produce very different row counts and downstream joins.

questions.q: What's the real trade-off of a snowflake schema at scale, compared to a star schema?
options: Less redundant storage, but every query now pays an extra join to reassemble the normalized dimension
Snowflake schemas always perform better at scale
Snowflake schemas eliminate the need for fact tables
There is no trade-off — they perform identically
questions.explain: Star schema's redundancy is usually worth it for analytics specifically because read performance matters more than storage savings.

questions.q: How does an SCD Type 2 update get implemented at scale, per this lesson?
options: As a targeted MERGE into a Delta table, not a full table rewrite
By deleting and recreating the entire dimension table on every update
SCDs are not possible to implement at scale
By storing every historical version in a separate database
questions.explain: This ties directly to Databricks Lesson 22's UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE pattern — designing for SCDs at scale means designing the merge.

questions.q: Why does star schema's denormalized redundancy matter for Databricks performance specifically?
options: Because Databricks's Z-ordering and file-size tuning assumes a denormalized fact table to be effective against in the first place
Databricks performs identically regardless of schema shape
Z-ordering only works on snowflake schemas
Denormalization has no effect on query optimization
questions.explain: Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 23's OPTIMIZE and file-compaction guidance assumes the star schema's denormalized shape to optimize against.
